name: Flashcard decks
title: A textbook section in, an Anki deck out.
description: Read every page at once and write cards straight from the source: questions and cloze sentences with the exact passage behind each one. No planner and no writer in the way; near-duplicates are removed locally and a sample of pages is audited against its source.
brief: Write flashcards from the supplied sources for an exam candidate. Make one card per distinct testable fact, threshold, exception, mechanism or decision rule; prefer many precise cards over few broad ones. Use cloze sentences for numbers, named entities and lists, and questions for reasoning. Keep every condition that changes an answer inside the card. Cite the source passage for each card.
inputs: Add the textbook chapters, lecture slides or notes you study from. Everything selected is read; nothing is planned.
stages: Read every window at once
Each reader owns a few pages, sees a few sentences on either side, and writes cards with span citations. A window that fails is reported; the rest continues.
Remove near-duplicates locally
Cards are compared by local similarity, never by a model call. A later card is dropped only when it matches one already kept, so chains of different claims cannot collapse.
Audit a sample
A quarter of the windows get one source-centred audit call that reports facts no card tests and cards the source does not support. Findings are attached, never removed.
Export the deck
cards.tsv imports into Anki; cards.json keeps every citation.
decision: Readers decide what each card tests and how to phrase it. Code decides window boundaries, citations, duplicate accounting, sampling and the receipt. Two model calls deep: read, then audit.
context: Owned pages + a few sentences of neighbouring context + the brief.
delivery: Anki TSV, JSON with citations, and a readable deck page.
revision: Re-run after editing a source: unchanged windows reuse their cards; the edited window and its two neighbours are read again.

name: Reference guides
title: Several sources, one place to find an answer.
description: Combine chapters, slides and notes into a guide organized around the questions people need answered. Useful for clinical differentials, technical handbooks and operating procedures.
brief: Build a reference for practitioners using the supplied sources. Organize it around presenting problems or operational questions. For each question, preserve the complete answer group, conditions, exceptions and discriminating features. Merge equivalent questions; keep variants when they change the answer or the decision. Explain conflicts using source authority. Use tables when comparison helps. Include source citations and record deliberate omissions.
inputs: Add the reference texts. Assign authority, supplement and historical roles in Projects; add a layout example as a form exemplar.
stages: Read source regions
Readers extract ideas and supporting passages. Slide text, tables and notes stay together. Readers can request missing source context.
Build an answer catalog
Group equivalent questions, give each idea an owner, and preserve the conditions within each answer group.
Write by question
Writers receive the shared contents plan, their assigned answers and supporting evidence. Chapters can proceed together.
Check and export
Review each section, repair flagged passages, and export HTML, Markdown and PDF.
decision: Grouping answers before writing gives each section a defined scope and gives reviewers a complete answer group to check.
context: Shared contents plan + assigned answer groups + source quotations + selected prerequisite evidence.
delivery: HTML, PDF and Markdown, with source citations.
revision: Request a change to one section. Its writer and reviewer run again; unchanged requests reuse saved results. Replan when the sources or goal change.

name: Podcasts
title: Plan the lesson before dividing the script.
description: Turn dense material into a script that explains concepts in a sensible order, uses examples and asks recall questions. Connect a speech adapter to produce the audio.
brief: Write an educational podcast script for a practitioner learning this material during a commute. Choose a coherent route through the supplied sources and divide it at natural changes in the argument. Preserve useful answer lists, exact quantities, mechanisms and exceptions. Explain unfamiliar terms in context, include brief recall questions and revisit important distinctions in a different scenario. Each section should build on the shared plan and assigned evidence. Return a script with speaker labels and clear transitions.
inputs: Add teaching material and select its source roles. Set the audience and listening context in the brief. Configure a speech adapter when starting the local app to produce audio.
stages: Read in parallel
Readers collect explanations, conditions and examples from their assigned source regions.
Choose the teaching route and the episodes
One plan sets the order, numbers the sections into episodes of about twenty minutes, and gives each section a spoken-word target and the evidence it needs from earlier ideas.
Write the sections
Writers share the route and receive their own evidence packets. Review and repair finish the script.
Render the audio
Each section is synthesized the moment it is reviewed. Episodes are assembled as separate WAV files, with the full programme beside them.
decision: Writers receive earlier planned ideas and their evidence. They can work at the same time because they share the intended route. A task that requires the actual preceding prose needs a dependency on that completed result.
context: Teaching route + assigned material + earlier planned ideas and selected quotations.
delivery: Podcast script per episode; one WAV per episode and the full programme, with a speech adapter.
revision: Revise the affected script section and review it, then render the revised script. The speech adapter caches identical requests.

name: Practice exams
title: Write the questions and test what the candidate can infer.
description: Build cases and short-answer questions with separate candidate sheets and marking guides. A model attempts each question without seeing the key, then another call checks the answer.
brief: Create a staged short-answer assessment for practitioners from the supplied teaching sources. Choose a coherent situation with consequential decisions. Each stage should reveal only the information needed at that point. State the requested response and any answer limit clearly. Write creditable answer items, mark allocations and acceptable alternatives in the examiner material. Include questions that require applying the evidence, interpreting new findings and revising an earlier decision. Preserve conditions and numerical criteria from the sources.
inputs: Add teaching sources as authorities or supplements. Use example questions as form exemplars. Keep evaluation questions in the held-out assessment role.
stages: Choose learning targets
Extract evidence and group the decisions or answer sets the assessment should test.
Plan and write the case
A common route coordinates the sections. Writers produce candidate prompts and examiner material.
Solve with candidate information
Each solve receives the current prompt and explicitly required earlier candidate prompts. The marking guide goes to a separate judge.
Export both views
Save candidate and examiner files separately, with answerability findings in the examiner report.
decision: The solver has to attempt the question using the information supplied to the candidate. The judge can then locate ambiguity, missing data or a mismatch between the prompt and the marking guide.
context: Writers: plan and evidence. Solver: current prompt and declared earlier candidate context. Judge: candidate response, marking guide and cited evidence.
delivery: Candidate and examiner files, plus review findings.
revision: Edit the affected section and run the assessment checks again. Questions that depend on revised earlier information receive a new candidate context.
